docs.title: Measured results (bench, 2026-11-02, SanDisk SU64G, Phase 1 breadboard)
docs.text:
MB = 1,000,000 bytes. Test 5 uses a pre-allocated 32 MB file; random reads are 2000 × 4 KB.

Measurement FAT32 "bootfs", 2 KB clusters, 12.5 MHz FAT32, 25 MHz exFAT, 128 KB clusters, 15.625 MHz (current) Integrity (test 4): 16 MB file + 2 MB raw PASS, 0 mismatches PASS, 0 mismatches PASS, 0 mismatches Sequential write, best 4.39 MB/s (32 KB) 8.45 MB/s (32 KB) 6.50 MB/s (128 KB) Sequential read, best 2.84 MB/s 3.82 MB/s 7.28 MB/s (128 KB) Random 4 KB read, plain seek, avg 21.0 ms 18.7 ms 1.27 ms (p99 1.59 ms) Random 4 KB read, fast seek, avg / p99 1.47 / 2.00 ms — 1.26 / 1.55 ms Streaming 32 KB / 20 ms, 10 s 0 misses, headroom 20% 0 misses, headroom 46% 0 misses, worst 4.9 ms, headroom 76% Clock sweep (test 8) all steps to 31.25 MHz OK (HS) leaving HS failed; later run failed at 25 MHz on response CRC 10.4 and 15.6 MHz OK; HS switch failed (response CRC)

Observations and open items:

  • exFAT with 128 KB clusters fixed the slow reads. On FAT32 with 2 KB clusters FatFs splits every transfer at cluster boundaries (at most 4 sectors per disk call), and the driver pays a read command plus a stop command per call. With 128 KB clusters, reads went from 3.8 to 7.3 MB/s, and random reads no longer need fast seek (1.27 ms either way).
  • Streaming is comfortable: 32 KB every 20 ms (1.64 MB/s, about 2.7× FLAC 24/96) with 76 % headroom.
  • Library bug, worked around: carlk3 v3.6.2 rp2040_sdio_rx_start() writes its DMA list terminator one entry past dma_blocks[SDIO_MAX_BLOCKS * 2] for a 256-block read, wedging the driver. FAT32 with 2 KB clusters never triggers it; exFAT with 128 KB clusters does on every 128 KB read. The HAL splits reads into chunks of at most 128 blocks (guarded_read in hal_storage.c), and a failed read latches the write fault so the card is re-initialised before any further write. Worth reporting upstream.
  • Command-response CRC errors (open): the same responses are misread identically every time: CMD13 calculated 0x7c vs received 0x7e, CMD17 0xcc vs 0xce, CMD55 0x64 vs 0x66. They always differ in the last CRC7 bit. They appear around clock changes and the CMD6 (High Speed) sequence, at fractional dividers (12.5, 20.8, 25 MHz) and once at 15.625 MHz during CMD6. They never appeared during data tests 4–7 at 15.625 MHz. They look deterministic (a response-sampling or decoding issue in the PIO/driver path) rather than noise. Not yet root-caused. Because of them, the default is 15.625 MHz in default-speed mode and High Speed is not used.
  • The 10 MB/s USB mass-storage target is not reachable at clk_sys 125 MHz with this PIO program (4 PIO cycles per SD clock → 31.25 MHz maximum, High Speed only). Best measured: 6.5 MB/s write, 7.3 MB/s read. Open item, no decision (options: higher clk_sys, a different SDIO PIO program, or accept a slower sync).
  • Leaving High Speed mode needs care: the card is quieted at the current clock (open write closed, not busy), the clock lowered, and only then is the card reset and re-identified, with up to three tries; the sweep test fails if the card cannot be brought back.

docs.title: Failure checklist
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / action Card ignores the first identification after a debugger reset A reset mid-transfer can leave the card in a data state; a power cycle always fixes it. hal_storage_init() makes up to three attempts; before the 2nd and 3rd it sends four CMD12 (stop transmission: no data, harmless to an idle card, ends an open read or write-multiple) at the 400 kHz identification clock, reads each response, waits 50 ms and logs storage: card did not identify, wake-up attempt N. Nothing is written. A missing card still fails in well under a second (about 0.65 s in all, 0.5 s more than with a single attempt); it is called once at boot, never in a loop Test 1: NO_CARD or init timeout Card not fully inserted, 3.3 V missing, CLK/CMD/DAT wiring (GP2-GP7), no pull-up on CMD, card not powered CRC errors, or tests pass at 12.5 MHz but fail higher Clock too fast for the wiring: lower the clock, shorten wires, check pull-ups on CMD and DAT0-3 Test 2: NO_FILESYSTEM No FAT/exFAT volume (blank card, unusual partition layout), or the file system configuration is wrong (sector size not 512, exFAT disabled) Test 2 slow Free-space scan on a big FAT32 volume is slow by nature; it is printed separately Slow random reads (test 6) Small clusters or a fragmented file; compare plain and fast seek Streaming misses deadlines Read time varies: look at the worst read time; lower the clock only if errors appear, otherwise raise it Test 4 mismatches Bus errors that slipped past the CRC, or a bad card; repeat at a lower clock Test 8 stops at 25 MHz / "High Speed switch failed" The card refused High Speed, or a command response failed its CRC (see the open item above); keep the default SDIO "Timed out waiting for data block" on large reads The library's 256-block DMA bug: make sure reads go through the HAL's chunked guarded_read Card unreadable on a PC after test 9 Check the partition table with a PC tool: one partition, type 07, starting at the allocation-unit boundary; see ADR-0008 "writes locked until re-init" or "write fault" A write failed or the card status after a write was bad; the card was reset, check wiring and clock A test says a file already exists An earlier run was interrupted; delete /neupod-test on a PC and run again

docs.title: Wheel input widgets
docs.text: One library for every place the UI needs the user to enter something with a click wheel: text (passwords, names, search), numbers, levels, choices and dates. Code: app/ui/input/. The model of each widget (app/include/wheel_input.h, wheel_input.c) is pure C with no LVGL and is unit tested on the PC (tests/test_wheel_input.c); the view (app/ui/input/ui_input.c) draws it with LVGL and feeds it the input.

docs.title: Key semantics (the same in every widget)
docs.text:
Input Meaning scroll change what is under the cursor: the character on the strip, the value, the highlighted choice, the field. Steps arrive already accelerated by the UI frame Select choose or type: types the highlighted key, ticks a multi-choice item, picks the choice, goes to the next date field Menu back: backspace when there is text before the cursor, otherwise cancel (a number, slider or choice cancels at once; a slider restores its old value) Play/Pause confirm and close Left / Right move the text cursor, or the date/time field, or step a number by one

A modal swallows every button (Menu never pops the screen underneath by accident).

docs.title: Widgets
docs.text: Widget Request kind Result in wi_value_t Notes Text entry WI_K_TEXT text pages abc / ABC / 123 / symbols (a key on the strip switches page), space, a show/hide key when masked, a done key; max_chars (code points), charset ANY / DIGITS / HEX; UTF-8 safe buffer and cursor (accented characters can be a later page); initial text Search WI_K_TEXT with search = true text like text, and change fires after every edit so the caller can filter a list live. A suggestions row is not built; the callback is where it would hook in Number WI_K_NUMBER number min, max, step, decimals (fixed point, value in units of 10^-decimals), unit ("dB", "min", "%"); scroll steps are multiplied by the wheel acceleration; clamps Slider WI_K_SLIDER number a number with a bar and a live change callback; cancel sends the original value through change so the preview is reverted. Settings > Display (backlight) uses it Choice WI_K_PICKER pick single choice from items[count]; multi = true makes Select tick items and the result is mask Date and time WI_K_DATETIME dt has_date / has_time; fields day, month, year (2000 to 2099), hour, minute; the day follows the month and leap years; Select walks the fields and confirms on the last one Letter jump ui_letter_overlay_* + wi_letterjump_* n/a not a modal: an overlay on a sorted list. While the wheel is turned fast (6 steps within 400 ms) a box shows the initial of the item under the cursor; it hides 700 ms later. wi_letter_first_index() finds the first item for a letter (binary search). Files shows it today; the library will use it

docs.title: API
docs.text:
#include "ui_input.h"

static void name_done(void *ctx, bool ok, const wi_value_t *v) { if (ok) use(v->text); }

ui_input_open(&(wi_request_t){
    .kind = WI_K_TEXT, .title = "Network name", .initial = "", .max_chars = 32, .done = name_done });

ui_input_open() pushes the modal screen on the UI stack (one at a time: it returns false while another is open) and calls done(ctx, ok, &value) exactly once, before the modal closes. Two rules follow from that:

  • Do not open the next modal from inside done. The modal is popped after the callback returns, which would pop the new one. Record the result and open the next step from the owning screen's tick (the Wi-Fi screen does this for SSID, then security, then password).
  • Strings in the request only have to live until the call returns; the result is copied into wi_value_t.

Live filtering for a future library search: search = true plus change = filter_list where the callback sets the list's filter text and refreshes the list model.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
Models are small structs (the text model is 90 bytes). LVGL objects exist only while a modal is open. A covered screen can free its rebuildable objects (suspend / resume on ui_screen_t; the list widget frees all its rows) and a modal calls ui_frame_suspend_top() before building itself, so a modal opened over a list does not add its size on top of the list's. LVGL pool use on the host (64-bit objects, pool 72 KB, about 63 KB usable), read from the tour (ctest -R input_tour), with the Extras > Input widgets list underneath:

Widget LVGL pool used while open Without a covering list text, password, search 46.8 KB the same number, slider 44.9 to 45.4 KB picker, multi choice 59.8 KB (a list in a list) date/time 46.4 KB the list screen alone 57.4 KB

The firmware uses 32-bit pointers, so the objects are smaller there; the figure to read on the board is the lvgl_mem= line of the monitor.

docs.title: Demo and tests
docs.text:
• Extras > Input widgets opens each widget and shows the last result.
  • neupod --tour-input --snapshots DIR (ctest input_tour) walks through every widget and writes one snapshot each.
  • ctest -R wheel_input runs the model tests: typing, cursor, page switching, maximum length, masking, charsets, UTF-8, cancel and confirm, number clamping and acceleration, picker wrap and clamp, multi choice, date validity including leap years, letter-jump index calculation.
  • Not built: typing directly on the host keyboard as a shortcut (the host key map reserves most letters for the wheel keys); the testbed UART keys drive the widgets like the wheel.

docs.title: UI mock-ups
docs.text:
Text, number, level, choice and date entry with the click wheel is one library: Wheel input widgets. Wi-Fi screens: Wi-Fi.

Target: the Phase 1 panel, 320×240 landscape. Each screen is an original drawing at the panel's native size (SVG, viewBox="0 0 320 240"); the look follows the classic click-wheel player layout — split menu with artwork, blue selection bar — lightly modernised. These are design intent, not screenshots of any existing firmware.

Click-wheel vocabulary used below: Menu (top button, goes back), Select (centre), Play/Pause (bottom), Left / Right (previous / next), scroll (finger on the ring).

docs.title: Main menu
docs.text:
• Scroll moves the selection bar through Music, Podcasts, Photos, Extras, Settings, Shuffle Songs, Now Playing. Scroll acceleration follows the Rockbox constants (4 counts per step, velocity-based acceleration).
  • Select opens the highlighted item. Menu does nothing at the top level.
  • Play/Pause toggles playback without leaving the menu; the right pane shows the current track's artwork and title, or a clock when nothing is playing.
  • Left / Right skip tracks in the background.

docs.title: Library — artists
docs.text:
• Full-width list; scroll bar on the right shows position in long lists. Fast scrolling shows a letter overlay (not drawn) so a 100k-track library is navigable.
  • Select descends (artist → albums → tracks); Menu ascends one level.
  • Right on an artist jumps to All Albums for that artist; Left returns to the previous level without animation.
  • The same template serves Albums, Songs, Genres, Composers, Playlists and Podcasts.

docs.title: Now playing
docs.text:
• Shows artwork (see Now Playing art), title, artist, album, the format badge (e.g. FLAC 24/96, wired, bit-perfect) and the progress bar with elapsed and remaining time.
  • Scroll adjusts volume by default; a first Select switches the scroll to seek (bar highlights), a second Select returns to volume. Pressing Select again shows rating / shuffle / repeat options (not drawn).
  • Play/Pause toggles; Left / Right previous / next track (hold Right to fast-forward).
  • Menu returns to the list the track was chosen from.
  • On Bluetooth output the badge reads the negotiated codec (e.g. SBC-XQ, AAC).

docs.title: Album browser
docs.text:
• Dark full-screen carousel of album artwork; the centre album is enlarged with a reflection.
  • Scroll flips through albums with acceleration; Select opens the centre album's track list; Menu returns to the library.
  • This view is the one place the UI uses the panel's colour depth heavily; on the AMOLED candidate the black background also saves power.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
• Two-pane: list of settings groups on the left, a live detail pane on the right for the highlighted group (shown: Bluetooth — connected device, codec, battery).
  • Select enters a group; inside, scroll changes the value and Select confirms.
  • "Click" is where the piezo / haptic / both / off choice lives (the piezo has no driver yet), and "Haptics" holds the actuator (ERM / LRA) and Calibrate rows; hardware decision in Requirements → Reused parts and mechanical.
  • "Output" chooses headphone / line / optical / USB when the jack detect cannot decide.

docs.title: Implemented (stage 2: home menu)
docs.text:
Firmware screens in app/ui/ (LVGL, light theme as in the mock-ups above; all drawing is original). Rendering is partial (two 320x24 strip buffers); the list scrolls with one short animation, everything else is static. Nothing persists across a reboot yet (settings are RAM only).

Common frame. A status bar on every screen: title in the middle, battery icon and percentage on the right ("--" when the gauge failed its check; green with a charge symbol while charging, red at 15 % or less), and a play/pause glyph slot on the left (empty: nothing plays yet). Menu goes back one screen (nothing at the top level), Select enters. Lists clamp at both ends (no wrap), the selection bar jumps and the list scrolls smoothly when the selection leaves the window; a thin scroll bar shows on long lists.

Scrolling. The wheel reports counts; 4 counts make one list step, and fast movement multiplies it (2x, 4x, 8x when many counts arrive within 150 ms; the constants UI_COUNTS_PER_STEP, UI_ACCEL_* are in app/include/runtime_config.h). Each testbed key press is exactly one step.

Screen What it does now Home Left list: Music, Podcasts, Photos, Extras, Settings, Shuffle Songs, Now Playing. Right pane follows the player (polled on every UI tick, and at once when Home comes back on top; the clock and card summary refresh twice a second). Playing a file: the 96 px art box shows the album art thumbnail (the note when there is none), then title (file name when there is no title tag), artist, and a play or pause symbol with the queue position (3 of 12, or just Playing / Paused without a queue; Finished once the last track has ended, and Error, Verifying or Verified for those player states, detail stays on Now Playing). Test tone: note, tone name, Test signal, play symbol. Nothing playing: the artwork placeholder, Nothing playing, the clock (--:-- until the time is set) and a card summary (type and size, or No card). Music Artists, Albums, Songs, Genres, Playlists; each opens an Empty - no library yet list. Podcasts, Photos, Shuffle Songs Placeholder screens saying what is missing. Now Playing Live: title, artist and album with track number from the file's tags (the file name if there is no title), a format badge such as FLAC 24/96, MP3 320k or ALAC 16/44.1, Playing / Paused / Finished or the error, elapsed and remaining time with a progress bar, and the volume with a level bar. The wheel is the volume (2 dB per step, starts at -30 dB); Play (or Select) pauses and resumes, and on Finished (or after a FLAC MD5 check) plays the same file again from the start, with sound; Right / Left = next / previous track of the queue (Previous more than 3 s into a track restarts it; Next on the last track stops and the screen goes idle); with more than one track queued the status line reads Playing - 3 of 12; Menu goes back while the sound continues. Without anything playing it says Nothing playing. Play/Pause works on every screen. Extras Files, Test tone. Extras, Test tone Three rows, each On / Off: 1 kHz tone, L/R ident (1 s left, then 1 s right) and Scale (C4 up to C5 and back, looping). Select starts or stops the highlighted one (starting one stops the other); Left / Right = volume; the screen shows the volume and the level reaching the DAC. Leaving the screen stops the sound. See Audio. Extras, Files Read-only browser of the card: folders first then files, alphabetical, hidden entries skipped (a name starting with a dot, or the FAT hidden / system attribute: System Volume Information, $RECYCLE.BIN; the host build has no such attribute, so only the dot rule applies there), size on the right, a chevron on folders. Select opens a folder, Menu goes up (at the root it leaves). Select on a .wav, .flac, .mp3 or .m4a (ALAC) plays it and opens Now Playing; the rest of that folder (playable files only, in the order shown, from the chosen one) is queued and plays on by itself, gaplessly when the rate matches; Right on a .flac verifies its MD5 without sound (see Audio). Other files show Not a playable file for 3 s; an AAC .m4a opens Now Playing with AAC not supported yet. At most 256 entries per folder are kept (... more (first 256 shown) row after them); names longer than 63 bytes are cut at a character boundary. Directory reads run in the storage task, so the screen shows Loading... and keeps responding; without a working card it says why (Storage unavailable: no card). Settings Two panes (groups left, live summary right). About: version, build hash, platform, uptime, heap free, audio blocks / underruns / jitter, core 1 stack, and the result of every boot check. Display: Select opens a three-row list: Backlight (Select, then scroll adjusts it in 5 % steps, never below 5 %), Auto-dim (Select toggles On/Off, default On) and Dim after (Select cycles 10 s / 15 s / 30 s / 1 min / 2 min / 5 min, default 30 s; greyed and inert while Auto-dim is Off); all saved on the card. After the idle time with no input the backlight steps down to 10 % (a set level below 10 % is left alone, idle never brightens); any input restores the set level at once and is delivered to the screen as normal. The idle clock starts when the menu appears. The backlight-off stage is not built yet (backlog UI-5). Click: Select cycles Haptic / Off today (default Haptic, which needs the haptic driver); Piezo and Both join the cycle once a piezo driver exists; saved on the card, and an older saved On/Off still reads as Haptic/Off. Haptics: Select opens a two-row list: Actuator (Select toggles ERM / LRA; a changed type calibrates itself) and Calibrate (Select runs the auto-calibration, about a second; shows Not needed / Not done / Running... / Done / Failed); see I2C peripherals. Gapless playback: Select toggles On/Off (default On); saved on the card; Off keeps the auto-advance but with the ordinary stop and start between tracks. Resume playing: Select toggles On/Off (default Off); saved on the card. Off: the last track comes back paused at its place. On: if the player was playing when it was last used, it plays on again at boot (if it was paused or stopped, it still comes back paused). Bluetooth: status (Off / Starting / On / Scanning / Unavailable with the reason), the local address and Scan for devices, which opens the Devices screen: it starts a scan as it opens and fills in live; its first row is Stop scanning / Scan again, then the devices found: audio devices (speaker symbol) first with a signal meter (see below), others greyed out, up to 12. Select on an audio device pairs with it (Bluetooth): the scan stops, the row shows busy dots and "Pairing...", then "Paired, no audio yet" (the device is now remembered; the link is not kept open until audio arrives in a later update, so it may drop by itself to "Not connected") or "Failed: " (not found, pairing refused, not a headset, timed out, link lost, radio error, busy or not pairing); if the settings store is full the first row says "Can't save: settings full" and the pairing is undone; the first row reads Cancel pairing meanwhile, and Menu cancels it. A device that is not an audio device says "Not an audio device"; with a headset already connected it says "Disconnect first" (one headset). Once a headset is remembered, three rows follow Scan for devices: its name (state on the right, with busy dots while pairing or connecting), Connect (reads Disconnect while connected and Cancel while working; greyed while a scan runs or another link exists) and Forget (Select shows "Select again"; a second Select within 4 s forgets the headset and its pairing key). The right-hand pane shows the radio state, the address, the remembered headset's name and its state. Nothing connects by itself at power-up (stage 3). Wi-Fi: on/off, status (name, address, signal as a meter), Scan for networks (opens the Networks screen: it scans as it opens; first row Scan again, then the networks found and the remembered ones, a name with * is remembered; each name once, with its strongest access point; Select on one starts the join flow, Menu goes back), Other network..., time zone, the time (set by hand if there is no network), Wi-Fi while playing; see Wi-Fi. Storage: card type, size, filesystem, mode, free space (computed by the storage task, computing... until done). Battery: voltage, charge, rate, state, alerts, gauge status; live, once a second.

docs.title: Now Playing art
docs.text:
The 112 x 112 box at the top left of Now Playing shows the album art of the track that is playing (the layout is unchanged: title, artist and album to its right, progress below, all at 320 x 240).

State What the box shows Track just started, art being found or decoded The dark box with a note glyph (the audio always starts first; art never delays it) JPEG found The picture, kept in proportion and centred, with the dark box as letterbox bars No art, PNG, progressive JPEG, damaged JPEG, picture too large (over 5120 px) The note glyph Nothing playing, a test tone, an error, or still opening The note glyph

Where the picture comes from, in order: the picture inside the file (MP3 ID3v2 APIC / PIC, FLAC PICTURE, MP4 covr; a JPEG is preferred to a PNG, a front cover to other types), then cover.jpg, folder.jpg, front.jpg in the track's folder (any letter case; that order). An embedded PNG is skipped without being read, and the folder is then tried. A JPEG that is embedded but progressive or damaged also falls back to the folder files. PNG and progressive JPEG need the PSRAM board (ADR-0013, amendment of 3 Nov 2026).

How it works: after the track has started, the storage task (core 0, the only user of the card) decodes the JPEG with TJpgDec straight from the card in 512-byte reads, shrunk by the decoder to 1/1, 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 (the largest shrink that keeps the long side at 64 pixels or more), one MCU row at a time, and averages it into one 64 x 64 RGB565 thumbnail (8 KB of static RAM); the whole picture is never in RAM. LVGL shows the thumbnail scaled to fit the box (1.75 times for a full-size thumbnail; soft edges are the price of the RAM). While it decodes, the task keeps the audio data ring topped up, sleeps 1 ms after every 2 ms of work (so input and UI keep running, the storage task outranks them) and stops as soon as another request is queued (it restarts afterwards). The result is kept for the album: a track whose folder, album tag and embedded picture size match the last one shows it at once, without decoding again. A big picture takes roughly a second or two on the bench (the card read dominates); the art: line on the UART gives source, size, scale and time. Decoder working memory (about 8.6 KB at most) comes from the heap for the length of one decode; if it is not available the note stays. Colour order: the thumbnail is native-order RGB565 like LVGL's draw buffers (the display driver swaps for the panel).

Click feedback. Every list step asks the haptic task for a click (ROM effect 3, a gentle click). The request is a non-blocking queue write: the UI never waits on the I2C bus, requests closer than 35 ms are dropped, and the driver goes back to standby after 2 s without a click or at any error.

Keys. UART testbed: w/k up, s/j down, Enter or e Select, m or Backspace Menu, a Left, d Right, p or Space Play/Pause. Host window: Up/Down arrows and mouse wheel scroll, Enter Select, Esc/Backspace/m Menu, Left/Right, Space/p Play/Pause. The wheel, when it works, sends the same events.

Signal meter and busy dots. Wi-Fi network rows, Bluetooth device rows and the Wi-Fi status row show signal as four small bars at the right edge instead of dBm: 4 or 3 bars green, 2 yellow, 1 red (the unlit bars are grey). Wi-Fi: 4 bars at -60 dBm or stronger, 3 down to -70, 2 down to -80, else 1; Bluetooth is 5 dB stronger (-55 / -65 / -75). The thresholds and the 3 dB hysteresis are UI_SIG_* in runtime_config.h; ui_signal_bars() (ui_logic.c, host-tested in test_ui_logic) is a pure function. The Wi-Fi icon in the status bar takes the colour of the joined network's bars and changes only after the signal has moved 3 dB past a threshold, so it does not flicker. A list row whose action is still running (a join started from the Networks list, a Wi-Fi or Bluetooth scan, the radio starting) shows four pulsing dots in the same place: set busy on the row in the list model (ui_list_item_t, alongside bars) for as long as the work lasts and call ui_list_refresh when it changes; the list animates it with one timer that runs only while a visible row is busy. The model owns the end: a Networks join ends when the station is up, the join fails, or UI_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS (the join deadline) passes.

Console log (UART). Every screen push and pop prints ui: screen 'Title' push|pop [-> 'Revealed'] depth=N lvgl_mem=used/totalB (modals too), and every list step prints ui: sel <screen> <index> '<label>', so the UI can be driven with the testbed keys without seeing the panel. Passwords are never printed: the text widget is not a list.

Host tour. neupod --tour --snapshots DIR walks through the screens by script and writes home, music-menu, music-empty, extras, files, files-sub, files-many, files-many-end, settings, settings-bt, bt-idle, bt-scanning and bt-found (the Devices screen), bt-pair, about, nowplaying (PPM) into DIR (the tour's key script predates the longer Settings list, so several of these names no longer show the screen they are named for; use --tour-bt for Bluetooth); neupod --tour-bt --snapshots DIR pairs the first simulated headset and writes settings-bt, bt-idle, bt-found, bt-pairing (busy dots), bt-paired (Devices, Connected), bt-saved (Settings > Bluetooth with the headset rows), settings-bt-saved (the Settings pane), bt-disconnected, bt-forget-asks, bt-forgotten, bt-failed (a pairing the simulated car kit refuses; ctest bt_tour); neupod --tour-art --snapshots DIR plays three one-track albums (cover file, JPEG inside the FLAC, PNG inside plus a progressive cover) and writes art-cover, art-embedded, art-none (ctest art_tour, checked by art_snapshot). ctest runs it as runtime_smoke against a small fixture card (build/host/fsroot_fixture, NEUPOD_FS_ROOT) and writes build/host/snapshots/.

docs.title: Wi-Fi: lwIP, the Wi-Fi service, the clock and secrets at rest
docs.text: Stage W1 of the Wi-Fi work (ADR-0007 keeps the radio behind hal_radio.h). Bluetooth is described in Bluetooth; the on-screen keyboard in Wheel input widgets. Not on the board yet: everything here was built and tested on the PC and compiled for the RP2350.

docs.title: Stack and memory
docs.text:
• The CYW43 arch is now the SDK's lwIP + FreeRTOS variant (pico_cyw43_arch_lwip_sys_freertos). BTstack is unchanged and still runs on the same async context (the radio worker task): cyw43_arch_init() starts the driver, lwIP, then BTstack, in that order. IPv4 only, no sockets, no TLS.
  • platforms/rp2350/lwip/lwipopts.h: static pools only (MEM_LIBC_MALLOC off), MEM_SIZE 6000, 12 pbufs, TCP window 4 x 1460, 16 TCP segments, 4 TCP and UDP control blocks. lwIP callbacks (DHCP, DNS, SNTP, HTTP) run on lwIP's own tcpip thread (priority 3, 2 KB stack on the heap (lwIP's FreeRTOS port takes the size in bytes; 1 KB left only 312 B free after a join on the bench)), not on the CYW43 worker; the SDK's FreeRTOS arch serialises the two with the async-context lock. Both, and the wifi task, appear in the monitor's per-task stack-free line, which is the number to watch. Country code GB (channels 1 to 13).
  • Cost (arm-none-eabi-size, whole firmware): static RAM 436,480 B (end of the Bluetooth work) to 476,968 B, +40.5 KB (after the review fixes: 32 settings tags and a second staging array, +3.4 KB), of which lwIP is about 28.9 KB (pbuf pool 18.4 KB, memory heap 6 KB, TCP and the rest), mbed TLS and the secrets code about 2.5 KB (arena 2 KB), larger settings tables about 2 KB, the rest the Wi-Fi service and UI. Flash 1,120,532 B to 1,214,268 B, +94 KB: lwIP, the HTTP client, mbed TLS (AES-GCM, SHA-256, HKDF), the CYW43 Wi-Fi code, the Wi-Fi service, the UI widgets. The heap is not measured on the board yet: new heap users are the tcpip thread (2 KB stack), the "wifi" task (4 KB), and sockets-less lwIP objects; the radio worker is unchanged at 6 KB (RT_STACK_RADIO, checked against CYW43_TASK_STACK_SIZE at compile time). Stack overflow checking is on (configCHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW 2). The monitor prints heap: free= min_free= every 10 s; compare with the Bluetooth figures.

docs.title: The Wi-Fi service (app/runtime/wifi_service.c)
docs.text:
One task, "wifi" (core 0, priority 1, 4 KB stack), owns the station side. It runs every 200 ms and handles requests from the UI (a queue, never blocking the UI).

Feature How scan hal_wifi_scan_*: SSID, RSSI, channel, security; one UART line per access point from the radio (wifi: bss 'ssid' aa:bb:.. rssi=-48 ch=6 auth_bits=0x05), one per network after merging (wifi: scan: 'ssid' rssi=-48 sec=WPA2 ch=6, strongest access point wins; never any password) and wifi: scan done, N networks. Names in log lines are printable ASCII only (anything else shows as ?). The driver reports only three bits (4 = RSN element, 2 = WPA element, 1 = privacy) and cannot tell WPA3 from WPA2 (both carry an RSN element), so an RSN network shows "WPA2" (the join still tries WPA2, WPA2/WPA3 and WPA3-only in turn), WPA1-only and WEP show "secured" (wifi_sec_from_scan_bits, host tested); a scan that the user walked away from (Menu on Networks) is finished by the radio by itself, and a new scan waits up to 8 s for the radio to be free instead of showing an empty list; hidden networks do not appear and are added with "Other network..." join WPA2-PSK, WPA2/WPA3 mixed and WPA3-SAE, open networks. The cyw43 driver supports all three; a join tries WPA2, then mixed, then WPA3-only, moving on when an attempt fails. Wrong password is reported as such and is not retried in a loop DHCP, DNS lwIP SNTP lwIP's client, default pool.ntp.org (setting NPns), resynchronises about hourly; the answer sets the wall clock remembered networks up to 4. SSID and a "has password" flag in the clear, the password sealed (see below). "Forget" in the network's action menu join deadline a join still "joining" or "no address" 60 s after it started (RT_WIFI_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS, wifi_join_timed_out() host tested, wrap-safe) is abandoned: hal_wifi_abort_join() leaves the network, the service logs wifi: join 'ssid' timed out (no IP after 60 s) and counts a real failure, so the normal backoff and auto-join retry. The state shows as failed (not "wrong password"), also for a join the user started. Found on the bench: after a reset the radio sat in "joined, no address" for over 10 minutes; on a marginal link (−80 dBm and below) DHCP OFFER/ACK frames are lost and the exchange can take 20–40 s, hence 60 s. DHCP is started once when the station interface is created (cyw43 dhcp_start) and lwIP restarts it on every link-up; the HAL does not restart it per join reconnect after a failure or a lost link: 2, 4, 8 ... up to 120 s between attempts (wifi_backoff_t, host tested); a user request or a success resets it; saved networks are tried in turn. With nothing saved nothing is attempted: the service only looks again every 10 s, and that is not counted as a failure (failures= counts real join failures and lost links) power wifi_policy_decide(): Wi-Fi is off while audio plays unless "Wi-Fi while playing" is On (default Off); the station is switched off after N idle minutes (default 10; setting); a scan, join, transfer or NTP resync counts as a need. The radio is shared with Bluetooth, and audio comes first diagnostics UART line every 10 s: wifi: state=up ssid=.. rssi=.. ip=.. ntp=1 saved=n reconnects=n failures=n lwip mem=used/size (max) pbuf=used/size (max) errs=n; Extras > Network test

The radio is switched with hal_wifi_start() / hal_wifi_stop(). hal_wifi_stop means "radio idle": the station interface is taken down (netif removed, link left) but the CYW43 chip itself stays powered, because Bluetooth runs on it; it is not a WLAN power-down and saves less current than the name suggests (measure it).

Settings stored: NPwf (enabled, during playback, idle minutes, zone), NPns (NTP server), NPtu (test URL), NPn0..3 (SSID records), NPp0..3 (sealed passwords).

docs.title: Coexistence with Bluetooth and audio
docs.text: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth share the CYW43439 and its bus, and lwIP, BTstack and the driver share the radio worker task. Mitigations: Wi-Fi is off during playback by default (the radio is then free for Bluetooth audio in stage 2); BTstack's controller flow control settings (btstack_config.h) limit what is in flight; the worker has a 6 KB stack. Core 1 (audio) never touches any of this. What to measure on the board: Bluetooth scan while joined, an HTTP transfer while a file plays (audio: underruns=), and the effect of "Wi-Fi while playing = On".

docs.title: The clock (app/net/sys_clock.c)
docs.text: hal_millis() stays the monotonic time for audio and timeouts. The wall clock is UTC (from SNTP, or set by hand in Settings > Wi-Fi > Time) as an offset from it. There is no time zone database: a zone is a base UTC offset plus "follows the EU rule". Presets: UTC, London (GMT/BST, the default), Central Europe (+1), Eastern Europe (+2). The EU rule: summer time runs from 01:00 UTC on the last Sunday of March to 01:00 UTC on the last Sunday of October. Tests check both edges to the second for 2024 to 2027 (ctest -R wifi_logic). The home pane shows HH:MM Mon 2 Nov once the time is known and --:-- before. There is no battery-backed RTC: after a power cycle the clock is unknown until the next NTP answer.

docs.title: Boot check and status icon
docs.text: The "wifi" boot check is ok when the radio driver and lwIP are up, not when a network is joined. A degraded check means the driver itself failed. "No network saved" is shown in Settings > Wi-Fi (status row and the right-hand pane), not as a boot failure. The status bar shows a Wi-Fi symbol: hidden when the station is off, grey while idle or connecting, green when up, red after a failure.

docs.title: Secrets at rest
docs.text:
What is stored: Wi-Fi passwords and Bluetooth link keys (and any later secret). How:

  • AES-256-GCM from the Pico SDK's mbed TLS 3.6 (Apache-2.0 option of its Apache-2.0 / GPL-2.0-or-later licence). Chosen over BTstack's rijndael because that is AES block encryption only: GCM (authenticated encryption) would have meant writing our own mode, which is the wrong thing to hand-roll. Only aes, gcm, cipher, sha256, md, hkdf and support files are compiled, with our own configuration (app/crypto/neupod_mbedtls_config.h), about 10 KB of flash, and a 2 KB static arena as its allocator.
  • Key: key_provider_get() (app/crypto/key_provider_chipid.c) returns a 32-byte key = HKDF-SHA-256 over the RP2350's 64-bit unique chip ID with a fixed application salt. The ID is the OTP chip ID read by the boot ROM before main (the SDK's pico_get_unique_board_id); it does not read the flash (on the RP2040 the same call talks to the flash chip, which would stall core 1; RP2350 does not). The host uses a fixed test ID. This is the only place that knows where the key comes from: moving to OTP or a secure element means replacing that one file.
  • Record: version byte, 12-byte random nonce (new for every write), ciphertext, 16-byte tag; the record's settings tag is the authenticated data, so a record cannot be copied to another tag. A password of up to 63 characters fits. Anything that does not authenticate (another neuPod, a card edited on a PC, damage) reads as absent: the Wi-Fi screen shows "password needed" and asks again, BTstack pairs again.
  • Existing plaintext Bluetooth link keys (from before encryption) are sealed on the first load. FAT does not scrub freed clusters, so the old plaintext may remain on the card in free space; the card is not safe for that old data.
  • Plaintext copies (the sealed value's plaintext, typed passwords in the keyboard widget and its result) are wiped after use.
  • NTP answers earlier than 2025-01-01 are rejected; the clock re-anchors hourly so the 49.7-day millisecond wrap is harmless.

docs.title: What this does NOT protect (read this)
docs.text:
The RP2350 has no EEPROM and no battery-backed NVRAM, and this firmware has no secure boot. The chip ID is not secret: it can be read with a debugger, and boards often show it as the USB serial number. So the encryption protects a lost or copied microSD card on its own; it does not protect against someone who has the card and the board (they can derive the same key). SSIDs are stored in the clear on purpose.

Production policy (design response, 3 Nov 2026; not built): on the RP2350 a random 256-bit key is written once to OTP at provisioning, using the OTP key page and page lock; the chip-ID HKDF above stays only as the pre-provisioning fallback. No secure element. An ESP32 / ESP32-S3 board uses an eFuse key and flash encryption under the same policy. Secure boot is a separate, later decision. All of this replaces key_provider_get() only. Writing OTP is irreversible: the provisioning step needs its own review before it runs on any board.

docs.title: Throughput test
docs.text: Extras > Network test: an HTTP GET (no TLS) of the URL in settings (default http://192.168.1.10:8000/test.bin, change it with Select on the URL row; serve a file with python3 -m http.server 8000 on the PC), body discarded, KB/s reported. It runs on the radio worker while audio plays, so the check is the audio: line. Not built: the variant that writes the download to an SD scratch file under /.neupod/tmp through the scoped write window (needs a ring between the radio worker and the storage task); today the target is discard only.

docs.title: Staged plan
docs.text:
Order (design response, 3 Nov 2026): W2 → W4 → W3. Library sync is why Wi-Fi exists, then OTA, then podcasts.

Stage Content W1 (done) lwIP, the Wi-Fi service, join/scan/forget with the wheel keyboard, SNTP and the clock, sealed secrets, diagnostics W2 (next) device HTTP API and a C# companion app for library sync (no TLS on the device) W4 over-the-air updates: bootrom A/B partitions with TBYB, image staged on SD, flashed only with playback stopped and core 1 parked in SRAM (ADR-0014) W3 podcasts through the companion; polish: roaming, AP list caching, captive portal detection, Wi-Fi during playback measurements, SD-file throughput test

docs.title: What to check on the board
docs.text:
1. Boot: boot: wifi ok : driver and lwIP up, bt: lines as before, Bluetooth still ok. Splash with both radios solid.
  2. Settings > Wi-Fi > Scan for networks (opens the Networks screen and scans at once): your networks appear with signal; Select your home network, type the password with the wheel (Select types, Menu deletes, the last key show unmasks, Play joins). The status shows the address and the signal; wifi: joined ... on the UART.
  3. NTP: the home screen shows the time (and the right zone, BST in summer) a few seconds after joining. Reboot: it is --:-- until the network is back.
  4. Power cycle: it reconnects by itself; the password is not asked again. Move the card to another board (or edit the file): "password needed".
  5. Play a file: the Wi-Fi symbol disappears (radio paused) unless "Wi-Fi while playing" is On. With it On, run the Network test and watch audio: for underruns=0.
  6. Settings > Bluetooth > Scan while joined: still finds the headset.
  7. Read heap:, lvgl_mem= and the wifi: line's lwIP figures after all that.
