docs.title: Architecture decision records
docs.text:
Format: Michael Nygard.

ADR Title Status 0001 RP2350 as Phase 1 platform Proposed 0002 Display: ST7789 SPI for Phase 1 Proposed 0003 Audio quality policy Proposed 0004 Donor platform: iPod Classic 6G (A1238) Proposed 0005 Firmware architecture: portable app over a HAL, host build Proposed 0006 Storage: microSD over 4-bit SDIO, exFAT Proposed 0007 Bluetooth audio path: BTstack or external transmitter Proposed (updated 3 Nov: no bare CYW43439 on the final board) 0008 Card format: exFAT with 128 KB clusters Proposed 0009 RTOS: FreeRTOS (SMP part amended by 0011) Accepted, amended 0010 UI toolkit: LVGL v9 Accepted 0011 Single-core FreeRTOS on core 0, bare-metal audio core on core 1 Accepted 0012 Audio codec for the final board (ES8311 / ES8388 / PCM5102A) Proposed (mono check open) 0013 Bluetooth stage 2 RAM on the testbed, PSRAM on the final board Accepted 0014 OTA with bootrom A/B partitions and TBYB Accepted 0015 Clock plan Accepted 0016 Gapless playback and the play queue Accepted 0017 Music library index Accepted

Every feature ADR carries a RAM budget line in its Consequences (from 3 Nov 2026).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text: neuPod needs a compute platform with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth (A2DP), microSD, I²S audio, a display interface and the iPod 6G click-wheel interface. Two platforms are being evaluated side by side: the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (RP2350 + CYW43439) and the ESP32-S3. A working RP2350 build already exists, with a Debug Probe for flashing and console.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (RP2350) as the Phase 1 testbed and primary platform. Keep an ESP32-S3 build of the same portable app/ sources in the repo as a comparison.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• microSD runs as 4-bit SDIO on PIO, and the click-wheel receiver is a PIO program.
  • Bluetooth A2DP uses BTstack on the CYW43439, with an external Qualcomm QCC module as the alternative.
  • Application code must stay portable behind the HAL so the ESP32-S3 comparison remains meaningful; platform code lives under platforms/.
  • Two toolchains (Pico SDK, ESP-IDF) must be maintained in CI.

docs.title: ADR-0002: Display: ST7789 SPI for Phase 1
Status
docs.text: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The Phase 1 testbed needs a display to develop the UI against. The final product candidates are the EastRising ER-TFT024IPS-3 (2.4" ST7789V, 50-pin FPC) or a 2.4" 450×600 AMOLED (RM690B0, QSPI), with the original iPod screen as an option.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use the Adafruit 2.0" 320×240 IPS TFT (ST7789, SPI) in landscape on SPI1 for Phase 1, driven with DMA, backlight PWM on GP8. The display is accessed only through hal_display.h.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The ST7789 driver carries over to the ER-TFT024IPS-3 candidate, which uses the same controller family.
  • The AMOLED candidate would need a separate QSPI driver behind the same HAL.
  • 320×240 is the UI's development resolution; the UI must not hard-code it.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text: neuPod plays local files in MP3, AAC, FLAC, ALAC and Opus to wired outputs and to Bluetooth A2DP sinks. Each processing stage is an opportunity to lose quality.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Lossless end-to-end on wired/digital paths.
  • Decode once, into a 32-bit mixer.
  • No resampling unless the sink requires it.
  • Codecs: MP3, AAC, FLAC, ALAC, Opus.
  • Bluetooth A2DP via BTstack (SBC / SBC-XQ) on the CYW43439; an external Qualcomm QCC module is the alternative.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• hal_audio.h takes signed 32-bit interleaved samples at the source rate and reports which rates the sink can run natively.
  • Bluetooth output is lossy by nature (SBC); the policy applies to wired/digital paths.
  • Memory and CPU budgets must allow a 32-bit mix buffer.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Proposed (decision taken 25 Oct 2026; donor purchased)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A replacement logic board has to be designed around one iPod family's shell, mid-frame, click wheel, display and flex cables. Candidates were the 4G (Sprout's target), the 5G/5.5G Video and the 6G/7G Classic.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Design for the iPod Classic 6G/7G, starting from a thin-shell 120 GB A1238 (EMC 2173, board revision A, 2008). The thick 160 GB shell is treated as a variant that only changes the back cover and available battery depth.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Cheapest and most plentiful donors (£20–40 with dead drives); same shell, screen and wheel across 6G and 7G.
  • 320×240 colour panel and the larger wheel; the LCD, wheel, PMU and codec interfaces are documented in Rockbox's ipod6g target.
  • The all-metal shell is a Faraday cage: antenna placement is constrained to the plastic inserts (headphone jack area, under the wheel).
  • Usable internal depth is ~6 mm (thin) or ~9 mm (thick) for board plus cell once the HDD is removed.
  • Nothing published gives the 6G connector pitches, board outline or mid-frame geometry; these come from measuring and 3D-scanning the donor.

docs.title: ADR-0005: Firmware architecture — portable app over a HAL, with a host build
Status
docs.text: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The firmware is written from scratch and two MCU platforms (RP2350 primary, ESP32-S3 comparison) are evaluated from one tree. Most of the work — UI, library index, playback, codecs, filesystem — does not depend on the chip; the radio, USB and bus drivers do.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• app/ holds portable C only (UI, library, playback logic, codecs, FatFs). It never includes a platform SDK header.
  • hal/include/ defines the hardware interface (hal_display.h, hal_input.h, hal_storage.h, hal_audio.h, hal_i2c.h, hal_power.h, hal_radio.h, hal_system.h).
  • platforms/rp2350/ and platforms/esp32s3/ implement the HAL with their SDKs; hal/host/ implements it with SDL2 for desktop development and tests/ runs unit tests against the portable code.
  • Day-to-day UI and logic development happens in the host build; driver bring-up on the Pico 2 W with the Debug Probe; radio, USB and audio only on real hardware.
  • The display is accessed only through hal_display.h so the stock-panel and new-panel drivers are interchangeable, and the radio only through hal_radio.h so the CYW43439 and an external QCC module are interchangeable.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Both platforms build the same app/ sources, so the comparison is like-for-like.
  • Every new feature must first be expressible through the HAL; platform-specific shortcuts are not allowed in app/.
  • CI builds rp2350 and host on every push; ESP32-S3 is allowed to fail until its skeleton builds.

docs.title: ADR-0006: Storage — microSD over 4-bit SDIO, exFAT
Status
docs.text: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The original 1.8" ZIF hard drive is removed. The library may reach 100k+ tracks and 2 TB; the card must mount on a PC over USB without special software; the display and the card must not stall each other during playback.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• One microSD socket, SDXC up to 2 TB, driven as SDIO 4-bit from a PIO program (GP2–GP7 on the Phase 1 testbed), FatFs with exFAT enabled.
  • SPI mode is the fallback only (same wires: CLK = SCK, CMD = MOSI, DAT0 = MISO, DAT3 = CS).
  • The card is on its own bus, never shared with the display's SPI.
  • The library index is cached (PSRAM on the final board, or an on-card database) so browsing does not rescan the card.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• 4-bit SDIO gives roughly 4× the throughput of SPI mode at the same clock and higher clocks; needed for library scans and album-art loads while audio keeps playing.
  • The PIO driver needs DAT0–DAT3 on consecutive GPIOs and internal pull-ups on CMD and DAT.
  • A 2 TB card stays on the compatibility test list; controller quirks are where iFlash users report trouble.
  • The display's own SD slot on the Adafruit breakout is not used.

docs.title: ADR-0007: Bluetooth audio path — on-MCU BTstack or an external transmitter module
Status
docs.text: Proposed — decision deferred to a bench comparison. Updated 3 Nov 2026: bare CYW43439 ruled out for the final board (see the update at the end).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: AirPods and most headphones need classic Bluetooth A2DP. The CYW43439 on the Pico 2 W can do A2DP source via BTstack, but only SBC/SBC-XQ (AAC encoding is licence-encumbered and heavy on a Cortex-M33; aptX and LDAC are not available in open stacks). A dedicated transmitter module (Qualcomm QCC3008/3040/5125, Microchip BM83) takes I²S in, negotiates AAC/aptX HD/(LDAC) and removes the whole stack from the MCU — which also makes the ESP32-S3 (BLE-only) a viable host.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Keep the radio behind hal_radio.h and choose between:

A: RP2350 + CYW43439 B: ESP32-S3 + QCC module C: RP2350 + QCC module BT codecs SBC / SBC-XQ AAC, aptX HD, (LDAC) AAC, aptX HD, (LDAC) Wi-Fi CYW43439 on-chip CYW43439 Extra parts none QCC module + antenna QCC module (two radios) Power (playing, screen off) lowest, ~80–110 mA ~110–160 mA moderate

after a listening test: Pico 2 W running BTstack SBC-XQ against a QCC3008 transmitter board fed from the Audio Pack, both paired to the reference AirPods Pro.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Phase 1 proceeds on option A so A2DP can be proven early.
  • Option B flips the processor choice (ADR-0001) to the ESP32-S3; option C is only sensible if the RP2350's PIO/SDIO advantages outweigh carrying two radios.
  • The policy in ADR-0003 is unaffected: Bluetooth is the one lossy path whichever option wins.
  • HFP (headset mic, neuPod as Audio Gateway) and future LE Audio support depend on the same choice.
  • Required roles (corrected 2 Nov 2026): neuPod is the A2DP source (the headset is the sink) and the AVRCP target with absolute volume; an earlier draft of the requirements said "A2DP sink" in error. Option A implements these in BTstack; with a QCC module the module's firmware must provide them.

docs.title: Update (3 Nov 2026, design response)
docs.text:
• The final board will not use a bare CYW43439. Two independent reasons: it cannot be assembled at JLCPCB (≈30 pcs at LCSC, no RM2 module listed), and the BTstack / cyw43-driver grant covers Raspberry Pi products (Pico W / Pico 2 W / RM2), not a bare chip on our board.
  • Remaining options, now the main open architecture decision:
RM2 module ESP32-WROOM-32E (original ESP32) ESP32-S3 Classic BT / A2DP source yes (BTstack, grant covered) yes (ESP-IDF Bluedroid, Apache-2.0) no — BLE only Assembly hand-placed JLCPCB JLCPCB Host MCU RP2350B the ESP32 itself, or as a radio beside an RP2350B needs a QCC/BM83 A2DP module
  • Review point: the design response lists "ESP32-S3 / ESP32-WROOM-32E (ESP-IDF BT stack)" together. The S3 has no BR/EDR, so it can only be the host with an external A2DP transmitter (option B above); only the original ESP32 runs A2DP on ESP-IDF.
  • Antenna: in the top plastic window of the 6G back, the only RF-transparent area (Requirements → Connectivity).
  • The testbed stays on the Pico 2 W.

docs.title: ADR-0008: Card format: exFAT with 128 KB clusters
docs.text: (Numbered like the other ADRs, 000N-name.md; the request called it ADR-0008-card-format.)

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR-0006 puts the library on a microSD card read through FatFs, and the card must also mount on a PC. The Phase 1 test card (SanDisk SU64G, SDXC, 63.9 GB) arrived formatted FAT32. Choices are FAT32, exFAT, or a mix. Constraints: SDXC cards are exFAT by specification; some lossless albums and DSD files exceed 4 GB; the player reads in large sequential runs and a library scan touches many directories; a cluster size that is too small makes the FAT large and slow to scan, one that is too big wastes space on small files such as cover art.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The project format is exFAT, 128 KB clusters, one FAT, data area aligned to the card's allocation unit (AU) as reported in the SD Status register (4 MiB on the Phase 1 card; 4 MiB assumed if the card does not report one).
  • FAT32 must still mount and work for every read and write path as a fallback, because cards often arrive that way and the player must not refuse them. Nothing in the player may depend on exFAT-only features; files over 4 GB simply fail to be created on FAT32.
  • Layout: MBR with one exFAT partition (type 0x07) starting at the card's allocation-unit boundary and covering the rest of the card in whole units; the exFAT data area is aligned the same way. This matches the SD Association formatter. FatFs f_fdisk cannot place a partition (it always starts at sector 63), so the firmware writes the MBR itself and then lets f_mkfs format partition 1 (FatFs multi-partition support is on; logical drive 0 auto-detects).
  • Formatting happens only on explicit request (storage test 9, typed confirmation) and the player never formats on its own.
  • Users are advised not to reformat the card on a PC or phone, or to use the SD Association's formatter, which also keeps the AU alignment.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• 128 KB clusters: large files (audio, albums) fill clusters almost fully, the FAT stays small (a 64 GB card needs about 0.5 M entries), and sequential reads stay mostly contiguous. Cover art and small files waste up to 128 KB each; acceptable because the library is dominated by audio. Revisit if the measured scan or space numbers say otherwise.
  • Formatting erases the whole card including other partitions (for example a Linux root file system on a Raspberry Pi OS card); the confirmation prompt says so. A PC should see a normal single-partition card; this still has to be confirmed on the bench.
  • Free-space queries (f_getfree) on FAT32 scan the whole FAT and are slow; exFAT keeps an allocation bitmap and is faster. The player must not call it in time-critical paths.
  • The 4 GB file limit and weaker power-loss behaviour of FAT32 remain for fallback cards.

docs.title: Evidence (bench, 2026-11-02)
docs.text: Formatted with hal_storage_format() (test 9) on a 64 GB SanDisk SDXC: MBR partition at sector 8192, exFAT, 128 KB clusters, 656 ms. Compared with the same card's 2 KB-cluster FAT32 volume, sequential reads rose from 3.8 to 7.3 MB/s and random 4 KB reads from 18.7 ms to 1.27 ms average (see storage). 128 KB clusters also exposed a 256-block read bug in the SD library, now worked around in the HAL.

docs.title: ADR-0009: RTOS — FreeRTOS SMP, audio pinned to core 1
Status
docs.text: Accepted (decided by the project owner). Amended by ADR-0011: the SMP configuration below did not work on the board; the kernel is now single-core on core 0 and core 1 is a bare-metal audio core. The FreeRTOS choice, heap, os.h, cyw43 variant and host POSIX port stand.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Playback must not glitch while the UI renders, the SD card is read and the radio is serviced. The RP2350 has two Cortex-M33 cores. The portable app/ code must run unchanged on the desktop build, and the ESP32-S3 comparison platform ships FreeRTOS natively.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• FreeRTOS SMP, from the Raspberry Pi fork of the kernel (lib/FreeRTOS-Kernel, submodule, pinned at commit 4f7299d, kernel V11.1.0+; the fork has no release tags), ARM_CM33_NTZ / RP2350 port, both cores, 1 kHz tick, heap_4 (112 KB), stack-overflow check 2, malloc-failed hook, run-time statistics.
  • Audio is one task pinned to core 1 at the highest application priority (7). Only the decoder may share core 1, at priority 6: it is the one large, bursty CPU consumer, and keeping it beside the audio task leaves core 0 free for UI, SD, input and the radio. The decoder is always pre-empted by audio and talks to it through a lock-free ring buffer, so audio never waits on a lower-priority task. Every other task, the timer service task and the CYW43 worker are pinned to core 0.
  • Audio timing comes from the sink's block clock on the 1 MHz hardware timer, not the 1 kHz tick. Today the audio task sleeps then spins to the deadline; waking a task from an interrupt on core 1 deadlocked the SMP kernel on the board and is not used until proven (docs/runtime.md, bench findings).
  • cyw43 arch: pico_cyw43_arch_sys_freertos (no lwIP yet). threadsafe_background services the driver from timer interrupts and its own locks, outside the scheduler's view; sys_freertos is the SDK's FreeRTOS-native variant: the driver runs in one worker task, created pinned to the core that calls cyw43_arch_init() (core 0), so its interrupts and work stay off the audio core, and BTstack (later) attaches to the same worker. (Chosen from the SDK sources; not yet proven on hardware.) Add the lwip_sys_freertos variant when Wi-Fi networking starts.
  • app/include/os.h wraps tasks (core affinity is a mandatory argument), delays, queues, mutexes, event flags and task statistics, so app code never calls FreeRTOS directly and times are milliseconds. One implementation (app/os/os_freertos.c) serves RP2350, host and, later, ESP-IDF.
  • Host uses the kernel's POSIX port (one pthread per task, one scheduling "core"): the same tasks, UI and boot checks run on the PC. Core affinity is ignored there and timing is not representative.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Core 1 isolation depends on discipline: a new task must pick its core in runtime_config.h; creating a task without a core is impossible through os.h.
  • Two builds of the HAL/SD glue exist on RP2350 (bare metal for the bring-up test executables, RTOS for neupod) because the SDK's FreeRTOS adapter changes the layout of its mutex type.
  • Panic path: stack overflow, malloc failure and assertions print the task name over the UART (lock-free) and halt with an LED code; on the Pico 2 W the LED sits behind the CYW43 chip and only blinks when the failure occurs in ordinary task context.
  • Tickless idle is untested in this port; power work later may need revisiting.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted (decided by the project owner)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The UI (split menu, lists, now-playing, settings, carousel) needs a rendering and animation toolkit that runs on a 125 MHz Cortex-M33 with a 320x240 SPI panel, and on the desktop for development.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• LVGL v9.6.0 (MIT), submodule lib/lvgl, every .c under src/ compiled with app/ui/lv_conf.h (derived from the v9.6.0 template).
  • One task only. LVGL runs in the UI task (LV_USE_OS = LV_OS_NONE); other tasks reach it via the capabilities struct, the battery store (mutex) and the input queue. This avoids LVGL's global lock and keeps its non-thread-safe API single-threaded.
  • Rendering: RGB565, partial mode, two 320x24 buffers (15 KB each); the flush callback sets the panel window, DMA-blits and waits (blocking for now; the second buffer allows async later); tick from the RTOS tick; its heap is a 64 KB static pool.
  • Fonts and widgets: Montserrat 14, 20, 28, 48 and the built-in symbols; only label, image, arc, bar and line widgets are enabled. Enable more when stage 2 needs them.
  • Host: the same LVGL renders into the host display framebuffer (PPM dump or SDL window).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Measured on the RP2350 build: about 0.45 MB of flash (code plus the four fonts) and 94 KB of static RAM (stage 1: 64 KB pool + two 15 KB render buffers; stage 2 raised the pool to 96 KB for the menu screens).
  • Assertions in LVGL go to the common panic path.
  • LVGL's symbol glyphs come from Font Awesome (CC BY 4.0 / OFL): recorded in LICENSE.md.
  • The drawing code must never be called from another task; use the queues.

docs.title: ADR-0011: Single-core FreeRTOS on core 0, bare-metal audio core on core 1
Status
docs.text: Accepted (decided by the project owner after bench evidence). Amends ADR-0009.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR-0009 chose FreeRTOS SMP with the audio task pinned to core 1 at the highest priority. On the board (Raspberry Pi FreeRTOS-Kernel fork, RP2350 SMP port, pinned at its newest commit 4f7299d) that did not work, in two independent ways:

  1. Waking the audio task from a hardware-alarm interrupt on core 1 (xSemaphoreGiveFromISR) corrupted the kernel: core 1 spun in vListInsert holding the kernel task lock, core 0 spun on that lock in PendSV, and the semaphore's wait list contained the audio task's event-list item twice.
  2. With the wake-up reduced to ordinary task calls, core 1 froze about 1.5 s after boot waiting in prvCheckForRunStateChange for a cross-core yield (SIO doorbell) that never arrived. A watchdog that re-sent the doorbell recovered it every time, so the cross-core yield requests are being lost. Every audio wake-up on core 1 depends on one (the tick runs on core 0). With the watchdog in place the audio period was still erratic (2 s outliers).

Upstream FreeRTOS-Kernel (V11.3.3) has no RP2350 port, and its core does not build against the fork's port, so there is no newer kernel to move to without porting the port.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• FreeRTOS runs single-core on core 0 (configNUMBER_OF_CORES 1, the RP2350 port's single-core mode): UI, input, storage, monitor, boot checks and the CYW43 worker. No affinity.
  • Core 1 is a bare-metal audio core, launched by the runtime (multicore_launch_core1 via hal_core1_launch) before the scheduler starts. Its main loop handles commands and runs the decoder; the output clock is a hardware interrupt on core 1 (the I2S PIO+DMA block interrupt on the RP2350, a timer-driven null sink as the fallback) that moves 256-frame blocks from a PCM ring to the sink. The interrupt preempts the decoder, so block timing does not depend on decode time.
  • Core-1 rules: no FreeRTOS or os.h, no stdio, no malloc, no SDK primitive that the FreeRTOS interop reroutes to the kernel (mutex, semaphore, queue, critical section, sleep, busy wait). Core 0 and core 1 communicate only through single-producer single-consumer lock-free rings and a seqlock: a command ring and a compressed-data ring (core 0 to 1), event rings and a statistics seqlock (core 1 to 0). The rules are enforced by a test (audio_core_rules) that scans the core-1 files for forbidden tokens, and documented in docs/runtime.md.
  • Layering: portable engine in app/audio/ (core side audio_core.c, control side audio_ctl.c); the block clock and the core launch in the HAL (hal_audio.h, hal_core.h).
  • Host: the POSIX FreeRTOS port runs the core-0 tasks; core 1 is a native thread running the same audio core loop, the block-clock interrupt is a timer thread, and the rings are the same.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No cross-core scheduling exists any more, so the failures above cannot occur. Audio timing depends only on the core-1 interrupt, which nothing on core 0 can delay.
  • There is no kernel on core 1: no RTOS timers, queues, or tasks there. A real codec running in the main loop must be written as an interruptible state machine with a bounded stack, and must follow the core-1 rules (no heap: all buffers static).
  • Core 1 interrupts and the RTOS share one vector table (the SDK points both cores at it); the audio core uses its own interrupt numbers only.
  • The kernel's SDK interop (pico_sync/pico_time blocking cooperatively) applies to core 0 only; the SDK's cross-core wake path for a non-RTOS core is not used.
  • A panic halts only the failing core.
  • The panic LED limitation of ADR-0009 stays; so does the host-timing caveat.
  • If a future kernel release fixes the RP2350 SMP port, moving the decoder back into an RTOS task is possible but not needed: the rings and the interrupt-driven sink already isolate it.

docs.title: Update (3 Nov 2026)
docs.text: Audio isolation is now a requirement, not only an implementation choice: a dedicated core for audio, bare metal, with lock-free rings as the only link to the rest. Any SoC candidate for the final board must have a spare core for it (ESP32 / ESP32-S3 qualify: core 1 for audio, core 0 FreeRTOS).

docs.title: ADR-0012: Audio codec for the final board
Status
docs.text: Proposed (design response, 3 Nov 2026). Open review point: the ES8311 is a mono codec (one DAC channel, one ADC channel). The baseline below needs re-checking against the stereo headphone requirement before it is accepted; see Consequences.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The testbed DAC is the Pimoroni Pico Audio Pack: TI PCM5100A (no MCLK, internal PLL from BCK) with a PAM8908 headphone amp on the "phones" jack (low/high gain switch); "line out" is the DAC directly.
  • The recording requirement (Requirements → Audio, 31 Oct 2026) needs an ADC; the CS43131 is DAC-only.
  • The JLCPCB/LCSC survey: CS43131 has about 42 pcs at LCSC, so it cannot be assembled in volume.
  • A codec that needs MCLK ties the clock plan (ADR-0015) to the codec; one that can run its PLL from BCLK does not.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The final board provides MCLK anyway: clk_gpout on a spare GPIO at 256 fs (costs one pin, no parts).
  • The codec must still run without MCLK (PLL from BCLK), so a clock problem never means silence.
  • Candidates, in order:
Part DAC ADC MCLK-free LCSC (survey) Role Everest ES8311 mono (see status) mono PLL from BCLK $0.43, ~100k stock proposed baseline Everest ES8388 stereo stereo needs MCLK (provided) stocked alternative TI PCM5102A stereo none yes stocked DAC-only fallback (recording then needs a separate ADC) Cirrus CS43131 stereo none — ~42 pcs dropped
  • Format: standard I2S, 32-bit slots (64 fs), as the testbed.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Requirements and Design move off the CS43131 (both pages updated).
  • If the mono finding stands, the realistic stereo-plus-ADC options are the ES8388 (or another stereo codec) or PCM5102A + a separate mono ADC (the ES8311 used as ADC-only would do). Decision returns to design.
  • A headphone driver is still needed after an ES83xx/PCM510x (none of them drive 16–32 Ω at useful level); pick it with the codec.
  • RAM budget: none (codec control is a few hundred bytes of I2C driver).

docs.title: ADR-0013: Bluetooth stage 2 RAM on the testbed, PSRAM on the final board
Status
docs.text: Accepted (design response, 3 Nov 2026).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Bluetooth is the primary output path. Stage 2 (A2DP source, AVRCP target) needs an SBC encoder and a core 1 → core 0 PCM ring (Bluetooth). The Pico 2 W has 520 KB SRAM and no PSRAM; after Wi-Fi W1 the static RAM is about 477 KB, so there is no free 32 KB.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Priority: stage 2 starts immediately after the Audio Pack tone test and MP3/ALAC playback on the bench.
  • Budget: 32 KB for the SBC encoder state and the PCM ring, on core 0.
  • Funded by:
  • sizing the codec arena as max(FLAC, MP3, ALAC), each measured at its worst case, instead of the fixed 116 KB; the arena never goes below the measured FLAC 24/96 need;
  • releasing LVGL's second render buffer while the display sleeps (BT playback is mostly screen-off), and re-acquiring it on wake.
  • Final board: 8 MB APS6404L PSRAM on QSPI CS1. Artwork decode, the HTTP client and AAC are PSRAM-only features; on the Pico 2 W testbed they stay out of scope.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The arena size becomes a build-time constant derived from measured figures; the unit tests that check worst-case sizes become the source of the number.
  • LVGL must be able to run with one render buffer (partial refresh only) and switch at sleep/wake without a redraw glitch.
  • RAM budget (testbed): +32 KB stage 2; −(116 KB − measured max) arena; −one LVGL draw buffer while asleep. To be filled with linked figures when built.

docs.title: Amendment 3 Nov 2026: album art on the testbed (JPEG only)
docs.text:
The owner decided to have album art now, on the Pico 2 W, instead of waiting for the PSRAM board. This amends the last bullet of the decision above ("Artwork decode ... PSRAM-only"); the original text is left as it was.

  • Scope: baseline JPEG only, streamed from the card (embedded picture in MP3 / FLAC / MP4, then cover.jpg, folder.jpg, front.jpg in the track's folder). PNG and progressive JPEG show the note placeholder until the PSRAM board. The whole picture is never in RAM: the decoder works one MCU row at a time and only a 64 x 64 thumbnail is kept.
  • Where it runs: core 0 only, in the storage task (FatFs is not re-entrant, so the storage task stays its only user), between audio top-ups; it sleeps 1 ms after every 2 ms of work (the storage task outranks the input and UI tasks) and gives way at once to any queued request. Core 1 and its closure are untouched.
  • Stays PSRAM-only: the HTTP client, AAC, and PNG art.
  • RAM budget line (testbed): static +8,552 bytes (8,192 thumbnail + 360 state; RP2350 .bss 476,232 to 484,784) and +17.4 KB of flash (decoder and glue; .text 1,221,776 to 1,239,184). Transient, from the FreeRTOS heap for the length of one decode and freed after: 4,096 (decoder tables) + a strip of 1 to 4 KB + 0.5 KB, at most about 8.6 KB, or the picture is skipped (placeholder) if the heap cannot give it. The static cost comes out of the roughly 27 KB that were free before, which leaves about 18 KB; stage 2's 32 KB above is still funded by the arena sizing and the LVGL buffer release, not by this.
  • Consequences: art_service must not be called from core 1 or hold the storage task for more than a few milliseconds without yielding; the 64 x 64 thumbnail is shown 1.75 times larger by LVGL (soft edges, accepted); the thumbnail buffer is a candidate to be reclaimed (or to become a bigger PSRAM-backed image) when the PSRAM board arrives.

docs.title: Amendment 4 Nov 2026: the Bluetooth PCM ring reuses the I2S ring storage (funding change)
docs.text:
This amends Funded by and the RAM budget line of the decision above; the original text is left as it was. It was agreed with the owner while planning stage 2a (Bluetooth).

  • What changed. The two funding sources no longer exist. The codec arena was sized down in #17 and that saving was spent there, and free static SRAM on the testbed is now about 15.5 KB (15,320 B measured on main at 4944981, __HeapLimit - __end__; 14,876 B with stage 2a). A new 32 KB budget cannot be found.
  • New decision. The core 1 to core 0 Bluetooth PCM ring uses the same 32 KB storage as the I2S PCM ring (NEUPOD_PCM_RING_FRAMES = 4096 frames, 32 KB). The two outputs are exclusive (audio goes to I2S or to Bluetooth, never both), so one set of bytes serves whichever sink is active; the ring is emptied and its counters reset when the output path changes. This adds no new static RAM. The 32 KB of the decision above is therefore withdrawn as new memory. What stage 2b still needs of its own (the SBC encoder state and its working buffers) is small, is measured when 2b is built, and comes out of the free SRAM.
  • Decimation on core 1. Hi-res audio is decimated on core 1 by a 2:1 or 4:1 half-band FIR to 44.1 / 48 kHz, with 24 to 16 bit TPDF dither, before the samples enter the ring (SBC carries 16 bit at up to 48 kHz). Core 1 keeps the ADR-0011 rules (no RTOS, no heap, closure-checked); the FIR's state and coefficients are measured with the closure check in 2b.
  • Wi-Fi during A2DP is allowed. Provisional, like the Wi-Fi-with-Bluetooth rule of stage 2a: one policy macro (NEUPOD_BT_WIFI_COEX_ALLOW), no interlock; bench testing may reverse it.
  • Consequences. (1) The LVGL render-buffer release while the display sleeps is no longer needed for funding; it stays a possible later saving, not a dependency of stage 2. (2) Changing the output path at run time needs a quiet ring (stopped or paused, as the audio engine already does to change sink or rate). (3) A Bluetooth link that drops mid-track must pause or switch the output back to I2S before the ring is handed over. (4) The closure check has to cover the new ring state when 2b adds it.

docs.title: ADR-0014: Over-the-air updates with bootrom A/B partitions
Status
docs.text: Accepted (design response, 3 Nov 2026). Two review points are listed under Consequences.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Wi-Fi W4 is OTA. The RP2350 bootrom supports a partition table, A/B application partitions and try-before-you-buy (TBYB) booting, so a custom bootloader is not needed.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Order of Wi-Fi work: W2 (device HTTP API + C# companion; library sync is why Wi-Fi exists) → W4 OTA → W3 podcasts through the companion.
  • Layout: bootrom partition table, A/B app partitions, TBYB.
  • Pico 2 W (4 MB): 2 × 1.75 MB app slots + 0.5 MB reserved (settings cache / scratch).
  • Final board: 16 MB W25Q128 (JLCPCB Basic part): 2 × 4 MB slots, rest reserved.
  • Rules:
  • the image downloads to SD as /.neupod/update.bin, checked by CRC32 and a signature before flashing;
  • flashing only with playback stopped and core 1 parked in SRAM under multicore lockout, never while core 1 executes from XIP;
  • the new slot boots under TBYB and is only made permanent after its boot checks pass.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Image size limit on the testbed is 1.75 MB; today's text is about 1.12 MB.
  • Review point 1: the partition table itself occupies flash (at least one 4 KB sector at the start), so 2 × 1.75 MB + 0.5 MB does not fit 4 MB exactly; the reserved area shrinks by that amount.
  • Review point 2: "settings cache" in internal flash conflicts with the current rule that settings and link keys live on the SD card and never in internal flash (core 1 runs from XIP; Bluetooth). Any write there must follow the same lockout rule as OTA, or the area stays scratch-only until decided.
  • Signature scheme and key storage are not decided here (ties to secure boot, which is a later decision).
  • RAM budget: download buffer through the SD write path (size set in W4); no new static RAM on core 1.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted (design response, 3 Nov 2026).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: On the testbed the ST7789 runs SPI1 at 62.5 MHz = clk_peri / 2, which is what fixed clk_sys at 125 MHz (display tests). SD uses an integer PIO divider from the same clock; the I2S divider is fractional (see Audio).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Testbed: clk_sys = 125 MHz; clk_peri sourced from clk_sys explicitly (not left to the SDK default).
  • Final board: the AMOLED is QSPI at 40 MHz × 4 lanes, so the panel no longer dictates clk_sys; revisit 150 MHz then (SD and I2S dividers re-derived at that point).
  • The codec gets MCLK at 256 fs from clk_gpout on the final board (ADR-0012).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any change to clk_sys changes the SD clock (integer dividers only, see Storage) and the I2S rate error; both must be re-checked.
  • RAM budget: none.

docs.title: ADR-0016: Gapless playback and the play queue
docs.text: Status: accepted (bench verification pending)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Tracks must follow each other by themselves, without a gap, for albums that were recorded to run on (live albums, DJ mixes). Until now one file played, core 1 drained and ramped down, and the next start flushed everything. There is no library database yet, so "what comes next" has to come from the folder the track was chosen in. ADR-0003 forbids resampling; ADR-0011 limits what core 1 may do.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Queue (core 0, play_queue.c): playing a file from Files queues the playable files of its folder in Files order, from the chosen one on (earlier ones stay for Previous). Non-audio entries are skipped. Next and Previous are hard starts (ramp, and a re-clock if the rate differs); Previous after more than 3 s restarts the track. The end of the queue stops playback and Now Playing goes idle. Static cost: 3.6 KB (names packed in a 3 KB pool, 128 tracks at most; a bigger folder keeps a window around the chosen track).
  • Handshake (details in docs/audio.md): streams get sequence numbers and live in two slots (seq & 1) holding the description and the stream's length in bytes. Core 0 announces the successor with AUDIO_CMD_STREAM_NEXT once the current decoder is open, and publishes each stream's length when its last byte is in the data ring; the successor's bytes may follow at once. Core 1 reads the ring before the length, so seeing the next stream's bytes implies seeing the boundary. A cancelled announcement is a cleared g_audio_next_valid, checked again when core 1 takes it over (copy, re-check). Everything is single-writer, no locks.
  • Core 1 switch: when the decoder has delivered its last frame and a compatible successor is announced (same rate and channel count), the decoder is replaced in place: sink, PCM ring and volume are untouched. The PCM ring position of the boundary goes to the block interrupt through a small SPSC ring; it reports END_OF_TRACK (value 1) when the block holding the last sample is served, so the UI changes tracks with the sound, to within one 256-frame block. Different rate or channels: core 0 announces nothing, the track ends the ordinary way (drain, ramp, re-clock) and the player starts the next one.
  • Encoder delay and padding: FLAC and WAV are exact. MP3: dr_mp3 already trims the LAME delay (+529) and padding (-529); the parser reports the same length (tested against the decoder, never trimmed twice). ALAC: the edit list (one non-empty entry) else iTunSMPB; the codec drops the priming and stops at the exact length, the encoder padding left in the stream is skipped to the stream end.
  • Setting "Gapless playback" (settings store, default on). Off: tracks still advance, with the ordinary start in between.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Static RAM +6.4 KB measured on the final build against origin/main (arm-none-eabi-objdump -h: .bss 0x75c18 to 0x77518 = +6,400 B, .data +152 B): queue 3.6 KB, second track context with both paths 1.7 KB, slots 0.3 KB, boundary ring and bookkeeping the rest. No extra codec memory: the arena is reused by the successor's decoder after the old one has finished.
  • The successor's header is parsed from the card while the current track plays (one 2 KB-buffered pass, with the data ring full).
  • Only one handoff can be pending: tracks shorter than about 0.3 s cannot chain gaplessly (they still play, with the ordinary start).
  • A decoder that needs more than the whole file before it opens (a file smaller than the 24 KB read chunk of the MP3 decoder) cannot be a gapless successor of another track earlier than its end is published: such a file simply falls back to the ordinary start.
  • Core-1 additions are small (switch, boundary list); core-1 closure checks pass.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• If the block interrupt stalls for more than 100 ms (FLUSH_TIMEOUT_US) during a flush, the loop proceeds and boundaries still queued may be dropped: a gapless track change would then not be reported (the next hard start re-synchronises). Not seen on the bench.
  • A folder with more than 128 playable files, or more than 3 KB of names, queues a window around the chosen track; the album then ends at the window's end without saying so. A later UI hint ("queue limited") would be the remedy.
  • The art service restarts its decode when a gapless handoff changes the album mid-decode (a job generation is re-checked after every yield); a same-album handoff costs nothing.
  • The player logs one line per track change on the UART (player: track 3/6 'name' (start|next|prev|restart|gapless|auto|skip|repeat|wrap), player: queue end; a handoff made by the audio core reads gapless, gapless repeat or gapless wrap).

docs.title: Amendment: shuffle and repeat
docs.text:
• Shuffle (off / songs) and repeat (off / one / all) are settings (NPsh, NPrp, default off), applied to the queue being played at once.
  • The queue keeps entries in folder order plus a play-order array (order[slot], 256 B in play_queue_t, no allocation); pos is a slot. Shuffle is a seeded Fisher-Yates permutation (xorshift32, seeded from the tick count at the user's action) with the current track at slot 0, so turning it on mid-play keeps the track; turning it off returns to folder order at the same track. Previous walks back through the shuffled order; more than 3 s in it restarts as before.
  • Repeat-one only applies when a track ends by itself (and to the gapless look-ahead, which then offers the same file again); the Next button still moves on. Repeat-all wraps to slot 0 instead of queue end; with shuffle it re-shuffles and never opens the new round with the track that just ended (unless the queue has one track). The opening track is fixed when the look-ahead asks (wrap_first), so the announced handoff and the later move agree.
  • The gapless descriptor handoff is unchanged. If a mode changes after the next track was announced to the audio core, the player records the announced queue entry and, when the handoff happens, pulls exactly that entry in as the next track (pq_commit) rather than trusting the new order. A failed start request after a move puts the queue back exactly as it was (a file-static 264 B snapshot of the order, taken only when shuffle is on; kept off the task stacks).
  • Turning shuffle on mid-play puts the current track at slot 0, so Previous restarts it (there is no history before it).
  • Under repeat-all an unplayable track at the end is skipped by wrapping, at most one lap in a row, so an all-broken queue ends in the error.
  • Cost: .bss +268 B (one queue instance) + 264 B (snapshot), flash about +3.3 KB. The main menu's "Shuffle Songs" stays a placeholder (needs the library).

docs.title: ADR-0017: Music library index
docs.text: Status: accepted (design note 4 Nov 2026; decisions D1–D6 taken 4 Nov 2026, see Decisions)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Music > Artists / Albums / Songs / Genres and Shuffle Songs are placeholders (app/ui/ui_screens.c:140-177). Playback today comes only from Extras > Files, with the ADR-0016 folder queue. Requirements: browse stays fast with 100k+ tracks, with the index cached in PSRAM or on the card (docs/requirements.md, Storage). Constraints:

  • RAM. Main SRAM is 512 KB and fully budgeted (app/os/memory_budget.h): FreeRTOS heap 80 KB, LVGL 72 KB, codec arena 99 KB, PCM ring 32 KB. PSRAM (U1 on the Waveshare board, APS6404L) is not fitted yet, and the design must not depend on it.
  • Card. exFAT. The card is written by Finder, Explorer and Linux, so the timestamps on directories can't be trusted to flag changes inside them. Every file I/O goes through the storage task (docs/runtime.md). Playback streaming takes priority over everything else on the card.
  • Tags. audio_tags_t (app/include/meta.h) has title, artist, album and track number only. A library also needs album artist, genre, disc, year, the compilation flag and the sort tags.
  • UI. ui_list already pulls rows from a model on demand (ui_list_model_t with count and get). A 100k-row list creates only the visible rows, so the index has to answer "row i of list L" cheaply. It does not need to fit in RAM.

docs.title: On-card index, immutable, rebuilt as a set
docs.text:
The index lives in /.neupod/lib/. Every file is written once per build and never edited in place. Files are little-endian, with fixed-size records, and each one starts with magic, version, count, crc32.

File Record Content manifest.bin 1 generation, the card fingerprint (D3), counts, CRC of each file, letter-jump tables. Written last. A build without a valid manifest doesn't exist dirs.bin + names.str 8 B directory table (parent, name offset), so a path costs a dir id plus a file name rather than the full string tracks.bin 32 B dir id, name offset, title offset, artist / album / genre ids, track, disc, year, duration (s), format/rate/bits code, playable code (0 = playable, else the reason: D6), file size, mtime strings.str var deduplicated UTF-8 string pool (titles, artist, album and genre names) artists.bin, albums.bin, genres.bin 16 B sorted: name offset, an 8-byte folded sort-key prefix, first child, child count by_album.u32, by_title.u32, genre_artists.u32 4 B track or artist ids in display order: album = (disc, track, title); Songs = title

The sort orders let each browse level be a contiguous range: artist → its albums → their tracks. Each list screen therefore holds just (table, first, count), and row i is one 16 or 32 B record plus one string read.

Estimated size at 100k tracks: about 3.2 MB of tracks, about 3 MB of strings, about 1.5 MB of paths and about 1 MB of indexes, so about 9 MB in total, which is nothing on the card.

Atomic rebuild. The scanner writes into /.neupod/lib.tmp/, syncs every file, writes the manifest last, then renames lib → lib.old, renames lib.tmp → lib, and deletes lib.old. At boot, if lib is missing or its manifest is bad and lib.old is valid, it renames lib.old back. If power is lost at any point, you keep the old library or get the new one, never a mix. The writes use the same write-lock path as the settings store (docs/bluetooth.md).

docs.title: Reader (browse)
docs.text:
• The reader keeps one FIL per open table, with FF_USE_FASTSEEK already on, and a small LRU page cache of 4 × 2 KB pages covering records and strings. The visible screen (10 rows) and the scroll window fit in it.
  • Fast-scroll letter jumps (docs/ui.md, Library) use the 27-entry tables in the manifest, with no search.
  • With PSRAM fitted, the same cache is simply larger (for example 1 MB), and nothing else changes.
  • Reads go through the storage task at a lower priority than stream reads, so browsing never starves playback.

docs.title: Scanner (build)
docs.text:
1. Walk /Music, or every root folder except /.neupod; TBD with D1. For each audio file, match it against the previous tracks.bin sorted by (dir, name). If size and mtime are unchanged, copy the old record. Otherwise parse it with the existing *_parse functions, after extending audio_tags_t: TPE2 / aART / ALBUMARTIST, TCON (including ID3v1 (n) genre references) / ©gen / gnre / GENRE, TPOS / disk / DISCNUMBER, year, TCMP / cpil / COMPILATION, and the TSOP / TSO2 / TSOA / TSOT, soar / soaa / sonm and *SORT sort tags. Artwork is unchanged (art_ref_t, not indexed).
  2. Intern strings without an in-RAM hash table, which would need about 160 KB at 100k tracks (about 20k distinct names at 8 B each). Strings spill to sorted runs on the card instead, and a merge removes the duplicates and assigns the ids.
  3. Sort. An external merge sort on keys of (12-byte folded prefix + 4-byte id), with 32 KB runs. Ties beyond the prefix compare the full strings from the pool, which is rare. Collation: ASCII case-folded; Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A diacritics folded through a small table; leading "The " ignored, as the iPod does; sort tags win when present; digits come before letters; everything else sorts by code point under "#".
  4. Write the tables, then the manifest, then swap (see above).

Estimated cost, to be measured on the bench: the walk takes about 0.2–0.4 ms per directory entry. Parsing a new or changed file takes about 10–20 ms: open, read the head (pictures are skipped by seeking), and for MP4 walk to moov. A first scan of 5k tracks takes about 1.5 min, of 100k tracks about 25–35 min. A rescan after adding one album is the walk plus a few files, so seconds for 5k tracks and under a minute for 100k.

Scanner RAM: the sort and intern buffers (32 KB) are borrowed from the codec arena, which is free while nothing is playing; the tag scratch is about 1 KB. That gives a static .bss cost of zero for the scanner, and is why D2 matters.

docs.title: Grouping rules
docs.text:
• Albums are keyed by (album, album artist). If there is no album artist, the artist is used, except for compilations, where the key is (album, "Compilations"). One album spread over several folders stays one album, and two albums called "Greatest Hits" by different artists stay apart.
  • Artists lists album artists (D4). Compilations gets its own Music menu entry, as on the iPod.
  • With no album tag, the album is the folder name (D5). With no artist, it's "Unknown Artist". With no title, it's the file name, as Now Playing does today.

docs.title: Playing from the library
docs.text:
Choosing a song queues its range: the album, the artist's tracks, all songs or the genre. That's a range in one of the order tables, so the queue becomes (table, first, count, position) instead of a list of names. ADR-0016 gapless and next/previous are unchanged; play_queue.c gets a "range source" alongside the folder source.

Library-wide shuffle (Shuffle Songs over 100k) can't store a permutation: 400 KB of ids. It uses a stateless keyed permutation over [0, count) instead: a 4-round Feistel network on the next power of two, re-applied until the result is in range (cycle-walking). That's O(1) RAM, reproducible from a seed saved with resume, and visits every song exactly once. The feat/shuffle-repeat index-array shuffle stays for folder queues of up to 128 tracks.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
Taken 4 Nov 2026.

# Question Decision Rejected D1 Who builds the index The device only. The device is the source of truth and validates the manifest. A PC tool writing the same format stays possible later if first scans of large libraries prove too slow A device plus PC tool now (two implementations of tags, collation and "playable" that would drift) D2 When the scanner runs Only when nothing is playing, with a progress screen ("Updating library… 1,234 / 5,000"), cancelled by Play and resumed later. It borrows the codec arena, so it needs no RAM of its own and cannot cause underruns. Revisit once PSRAM is fitted In the background during playback (~32 KB more RAM, competes with the stream pump for the card) D3 How changes are noticed at boot Fingerprint (volume serial number plus free-cluster count; walk only if it differs) plus a manual Settings > Update library that forces a walk. A miss needs a write that changes no cluster count (for example an in-place retag inside the tag padding) A full walk every boot (tens of seconds at 100k); manual only D4 Artists list Album artists, falling back to the track artist; compilations (TCMP / cpil, or album artist "Various Artists") under their own Compilations menu, as on the iPod Every track artist D5 Missing album tag The folder name as the album, so libraries organised by folder still browse sensibly "Unknown Album" D6 Files the device can't play (AAC, more than 2 channels, 32-bit ALAC, bad headers) Listed, greyed out. See the D6 notes below Leaving them out, with a count in About

docs.title: D6 notes
docs.text:
• The scanner indexes every audio file it recognises by extension or header and stores a playable code in the track record (0 = playable; otherwise codec unsupported, too many channels, unsupported bit depth, damaged header). Their tags are parsed as normal, so they sort, group and count like any other track.
  • Rows for them are drawn greyed out. Select shows the reason ("Can't play: AAC") instead of opening the track.
  • Queues skip them: auto-advance and Next / Previous move to the next playable record in the order table, and Shuffle Songs steps the Feistel permutation on past them, just as it already cycle-walks past ids out of range (one 32 B record read per skipped id, through the page cache). Every skip loop is bounded by the queue length, so a queue with no playable record stops with "Nothing playable here".
  • Counts (Artists > n songs, About) show playable and total ("1,204 songs, 37 can't play").
  • The manifest records a decoder-set version (bumped by firmware that adds a codec or lifts a limit). On a mismatch the next idle scan re-checks only the records with a non-zero playable code, so new codec support un-greys tracks without a full rebuild.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• RAM budget: reader about 10 KB (2 KB of open FILs plus 8 KB of page cache) from the FreeRTOS heap, so check the heap margin (runtime monitor) before merging. Scanner: 0 B static, 32 KB borrowed from the codec arena while idle. Library queue: 16 B instead of a 3 KB name pool. Flash: about 12–15 KB for the scanner, reader and collation table (estimate).
  • Phasing, one PR each: L1 tag extension + walker + index writer + reader, host-tested on a FatFs disk image with a synthetic tree of 100k entries; L2 the Artists / Albums / Songs / Genres / Compilations screens, letter jump, play from library; L3 incremental rescan, fingerprint and progress UI; L4 M3U/M3U8 playlists, Shuffle Songs (Feistel), album browser.
  • The Files browser and the folder queue stay as they are, as the fallback while the index is missing or being built.
